text: Exact-answer accuracy is 80% with the answer document first, 52% in the middle and 78% last on a fixed set of 100 questions. The middle layout has the lowest score, while the first and last layouts differ by two percentage points. These three measurements describe how performance varies across the evaluated document arrangements. The findings do not identify an internal neural mechanism and remain limited to the tested task and document length, rather than all long-context workloads.

text: Compact indexing returns an exact match for 89 of the 100 evaluated queries, compared with 85 for the baseline on the same fixed dataset. Its median query time is 150 ms rather than 120 ms on one device. The comparison therefore pairs a higher observed match count with slower median queries, rather than a uniform improvement on both measures. The counts and timings describe this dataset and device; no sampling uncertainty or production evaluation is reported. The result is an observed accuracy-time tradeoff, not a guarantee about deployment behavior.

text: The optimization accelerates one device kernel rather than the whole request by a factor of two. On the same batch and device with unchanged outputs, kernel time falls from 16 to 8 ms. Separately instrumented request latency, including preprocessing, transfers and postprocessing, falls from 112 to 104 ms. The component saving is therefore visible end to end as an 8 ms reduction, but the remaining request work prevents a twofold overall acceleration. These results concern the measured request configuration; the study does not evaluate concurrent-user throughput, and the reported profile does not establish performance on another device.

Since those blocks need not be adjacent, a sequence can extend without copying its earlier blocks into a contiguous region. Access follows the map to the required location despite the physical separation. The operation therefore explains how extension avoids relocation, rather than asserting that this implementation is faster. No performance comparison is available.
